static_traits.name: Lin Ke
static_traits.family_status: Lives with the husband, has a cat named KJ (currently lost)
static_traits.social_status: Social support comes mainly from her husband, but she feels he cannot yet fully understand her emotions; other interpersonal matters not mentioned
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems in the past, no psychotherapy received yet, No major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent logic, steady speech rate; obvious self-blame and negative emotions; fairly good cooperativeness

basic_info.main_problem: After the cat (KJ) went missing, strong guilt and self-blame persistently appeared, repeatedly believing I am a 'terrible pet parent' and blaming all responsibility on myself; this event significantly affected daily routine and emotions.
basic_info.core_demands: Hopes to deal with the guilt and self-blame triggered by the cat going missing and improve mental health.

core_beliefs: I am an incompetent pet parent

special_situations.event: The cat KJ slipped out the door and got lost when Lin Ke came home from work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I had not stopped the cat from running out in time, it means I am not fit to be a pet parent, I failed
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubling searching, contacting neighbors, posting flyers to make up for the 'mistake'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It is all my fault, I don't deserve to have a cat

special_situations.event: Repeatedly picturing the cat getting lost while alone in the quiet night
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I must stay perfect and highly vigilant at all times; if I am not careful enough, something terrible will happen
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Uses self-criticism and rumination to 'take responsibility', or briefly distracts attention with TV/social media
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should be more careful; I should do better

special_situations.event: Ongoing fruitless searching (posting flyers, asking neighbors but without leads)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If effort doesn't pay off immediately, it proves I am incapable and things will only get worse
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Further intensifies searching and self-reproach; hard to stop and rest
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It's over now; I may never find KJ

special_situations.event: Feeling that my husband cannot yet fully understand my emotions after talking with him
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If he doesn't fully understand my feelings, it means the problem is all mine and my feelings are unreasonable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Seeks less comfort from his partner and takes more responsibility onto himself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: He doesn't understand me, and it's still my fault

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be understood and recognized as a competent and responsible caregiver
core_conflict.fear: Fearing that failure will hurt loved ones and bring blame/negation, proving my incompetence
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of control and a 'responsible' self-image through excessive self-criticism and taking all responsibility upon himself

object_relations.self_representation: A failed caregiver who is at fault and deserves blame
object_relations.object_representation: Bystanders (like a partner) who don't understand my emotions

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When others (such as the counselor or partner) try to soften self-blame, raise external factors, or affirm their efforts
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Seeing others' understanding and balance as 'making excuses for myself / being irresponsible', fearing the loss of moral standing and control
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing 'It is all my fault / I don't deserve it' in a self-reproachful tone, avoiding acknowledging external factors; tone is harsh, language absolutist.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to see their own efforts and care (such as searching, posting flyers) and to do a more balanced reality test
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing that 'not blaming myself intensely equals being irresponsible', using reasoning to sustain self-blame
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using the argument 'letting myself off too easily without self-blame' to reject more balanced views; tone is firm, repeating 'should' statements.

manifestations: Feeling that my partner cannot yet fully understand my emotional experience
Self-blame and rumination markedly worse when alone at night

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently using harshly self-critical language (e.g. 'It is all my fault' 'I don't deserve a cat')
Worrying that 'letting myself off' would equal irresponsibility, hence persistent self-criticism

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: Distracting attention with TV or social media when guilty thoughts surge
Briefly avoids facing the core emotions brought by the cat going missing

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Heavy use of 'should' statements ('I should have been more careful' 'I should have done better')
Viewing perfection and constant vigilance as absolute requirements for a caregiver

positive_force: Has strong love and a sense of responsibility toward pets
Proactively takes action (searching, contacting neighbors, posting flyers)
Willing to seek help and enter counseling, open to change
Able to show empathy to others (can tell a friend 'it's not your fault')
negative_force: Worsening rumination when alone at night
Insufficient self-compassion, feeling misunderstood by important others

target_behavior.behavior: Intense rumination and self-blame appearing at night
antecedent: Thinking of the scene where the cat goes missing
Feeling misunderstood after discussing this with my husband
target_behavior.core_reason: Influenced by black-and-white and personalizing cognition, attributes all responsibility for a single mistake to themselves, and uses self-blame to maintain a self-image of 'responsibility and a sense of control'
target_behavior.function: Self-punishment to maintain a sense of responsibility and control; tries to prevent further mistakes through rumination (but it backfires)
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood, difficulty concentrating, disrupted daily routine, ongoing pain

target_behavior.behavior: When guilt surges, uses TV or social media for avoidant distraction
antecedent: When guilt and self-blame thoughts become overwhelming
target_behavior.core_reason: Tries to quickly relieve emotional pain and avoid directly facing feelings about the lost cat event
target_behavior.consequence: Only brief relief; the core issue remains unaddressed, self-blame and rumination then intensify
